Advances in topological superconductivity

Topological superconductors host Majorana bound states that are robust against local perturbations. Recent experiments on hybrid nanowire devices and iron-based superconductors have reported zero-bias conductance peaks consistent with these exotic quasiparticles.

This review summarizes material platforms, measurement protocols, and open questions for scalable topological quantum computing. We emphasize the need for improved disorder control and unambiguous braiding demonstrations before device-scale applications become realistic.

Complementary theory work clarifies the parameter regimes where topological gaps remain large enough for practical qubit operation at dilution-fridge temperatures, including estimates of coherence times under realistic noise.
